newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares reverse early gain to end slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares reverse early gain to end slightly lower.

text.p: * New Zealand shares reverse early gain to end lower
* Afternoon selling in Telecom depresses market
* Lion bucks trend to end higher, makes up Monday's loss
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
304 +2 * NZSC cap index +0.67 at 5,041.34
288 -2 * NZSE-10 cap index -3.56 at 1,096.29 330 +8 * Volume NZ$60.9 million. Futures -7 at 1,112
648 -7 * Other movers - +10 +10
Afternoon selling in Telecom reversed earlier strength and made for a slightly weaker close on the New Zealand share market on Tuesday.
Overall, activity suggested portfolio repositioning rather than any wholesale buying or selling.

"It doesn't feel like it's going to run away on the upside. It still feels pretty sluggish," Tim Snedden at ANZ Securities said. The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended 3.66 points lower at 2,220.27, off its seesion peak of 2,232.85.

Telecom, after hitting a high for the day of NZ$6.61, was sold in the afternoon, with several large lines being done through J.B. Were. Telecom made up just under half the day's total turnover of NZ$60.9 million.
Telecom's share buyback appeared to be having the reverse effect of what investors would normally expect. "That begs the question as to what happens when they pull out," Snedden said.
Overall, trade was patchy. Lion Nathan bucked the trend to close eight cents higher at NZ$3.30, suggesting the stock may have been oversold on Monday, brokers said.
Among other issues, Fisher and Paykel dropped 10 to NZ$5.10 and INL, which went ex an 11 cent dividend on Monday, shed nine to NZ$6.50.

Port companies fared well, with Northland Port gaining 10 to NZ$3.40, a record high. Ports of Auckland firmed five to NZ$6.30 and Port of Tauranga was well bid at $3.40. Turnover in all three suggested purely retail activity.
Printing group McCollam gained 10 to NZ$2.59, a line of 743,000 trading at NZ$2.60 a share.
